overall_structure.value: Aged (450 °C, 24 h) state of Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl. XRD screening of this alloy family shows the phase assembly is Al-dependent: ferrite (α) content increases with rising Al (2–11 wt.%); the increasing ferrite content is reported to be more relevant for the strength/ductility trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite. XRD legend for this family also includes ε martensite and κ carbide, with κ carbide appearing at 600 °C in the highest-Al alloy.

source.reason: Aged-state phase assembly of the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl sample (450 °C, 24 h) from family-level XRD screening.

unmapped_findings: The Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family comprises five alloys with Al varying over 2–11 wt.%, but the individual Al levels are not enumerated in the paper, so the exact Al content of this 450 °C/24 h aged sample cannot be identified [b0019, b0109].
The as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure (state before hot rolling) [b0021].

For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl system, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops as Al content increases from 2 to 11 wt.%; XRD screening attributes this trend mainly to increasing ferrite content rather than to κ-carbides or ε-martensite [b0026].

Fig. 6 plots mechanical (YS, UTS, TE, hardness) and XRD phase data for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl system only for as-quenched, 400 °C/24 h, 500 °C/24 h and 600 °C/24 h conditions; the 450 °C/24 h condition (this sample) is not plotted, so no sample-specific YS/UTS/TE/HBW values are reported for the 450 °C/24 h aged condition [figure_006].

The paper states that κ-carbides in Fe-Mn-Al-C steels form either at 500–600 °C or during quenching for >10 wt.% Al; no κ-carbide formation is specifically reported for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family aged at 450 °C/24 h [b0004, b0026].
Tensile testing was conducted at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, and all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state [b0020].
